# 大规模GEO：跨AI搜索引擎衡量品牌可见度

**原题：**Generative Engine Optimization at Scale: Measuring Brand Visibility Across AI Search Engines  
**作者：**Pratyush Kumar，Ranqo（亦称Ranqo AI），pratyush@ranqo.ai，ranqo.ai。  
**版本：**arXiv:2606.20065v1，2026年6月18日，14页。  
**状态：**全文翻译与教学初校，正文1—9、致谢/利益声明、附录A/B、4张编号表及全部无编号表、公式和15条书目保留。商业生产库与代码未公开，译者未复算。所有“v1.1方案”是尚未完成的研究计划，非已验证优化收益。

## 第一部分：全文中文译文

### 摘要

传统蓝链接时代近年明显变化：人们不只向Google/Bing输入查询，也向ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini等AI搜索提问。曾专注SEO的品牌，现在还需争取在AI引擎中有效呈现。GEO、AEO、AI Search Visibility等新词都关心品牌如何被表述、引用、推荐；这些引擎用LLM收集处理互联网信息。本文将AEO和AI可见度纳入GEO。

本文解释如何跨引擎衡量可见度、分析回答，考察它们引用品牌时看重什么、依赖何种来源、哪些内容较可能被处理与呈现。已有权威的大品牌自然常被引，更困难重要的是中小企业、D2C、创作者、早期创业、网上足迹少的品牌。

基于Ranqo2026年3—5月100多个品牌、10万余回答：首次运行形成三档地位阶梯，Stripe/Nike等全球名牌在相关回答中出现73%，Olipop/Klaviyo等成熟中型/区域品牌44%，小众小品牌11%，逐档约差30个百分点。有来源时约78%引用去企业站，含自家与同行第三方；非企业来源YouTube最高，超Reddit、编辑媒体、Wikipedia。页级最高杠杆是排名式“最佳X”榜单，约全部引用21%；一页可在多个答案带出品牌。情感不稳定，正负框架翻转约比有无提及频繁6.7倍。

这些给出首批大规模GEO基线：可见度可测、因平台和成熟度异。末尾提出七项v1.1方案测试建议能否因果改善。面向初学者、实践者、创始人、营销者、研究者，希望帮助衡量、比较、改善AI品牌可见度。

关键词：GEO、AEO、AI搜索可见度、AI优化内容、LLM、引用分析、品牌可见度、声量份额、ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity/Gemini/Grok、E-E-A-T、多平台测量、Ranqo。

### 1 引言

越来越多人直接问AI买什么、用什么工具、信谁，而不翻十条链接。品牌问题从“某关键词排名多少”变成“用户问品类时模型会不会点我名”。GEO是衡量改善AI如何表述、引用、推荐品牌[本文引Aggarwal2024]；AEO/AI可见度是相近视角，本文归于GEO。它不替代SEO，而建立其上，因为AI摄取多数仍是原为搜索发布的内容。

大且权威品牌通常无论如何会被引，未解难题属于中小、D2C、创作者、初创、足迹少者，是本文重点。研究显示AI玩法不同于传统SEO：来源更广更异、内部知识依赖不一（Kirsten）；引用集中且平台选不同媒体（Yang）；已高引来源受偏好，马太效应（Algaba）；首个会话SEO系统基准发现多数战术无效、有些有害（Puerto）。本文用生产数据接续。

**贡献：**

1. 生产测量法：介绍Ranqo对五引擎受控查询，测是否提及、次序、框架、竞争声量，分类来源，六维查页，周期复测。
2. 品类参照：已发布CRM研究，50无品牌提示×五引擎×十次=2500回答、十CRM品牌。
3. 生产发现：首日识别；提及多近确定、无干预轨迹平；自家站占小、他公司占大；情感比提及嘈杂；核心地位阶梯。
4. 小品牌实践解读与七项v1.1因果测试计划。

以下第2节相关研究，第3平台，第4方法，第5CRM，第6发现及计划，第7讨论，第8限制，第9结论。

### 2 背景与相关工作

#### 2.1 术语

按Ranqo实务用法：SEO是经典蓝链接排名；AEO是成为精选摘要/直接答案框拉取的单一来源；GEO是LLM综合多来源时被引推荐；AI Visibility更广，看实体是否存在模型参数、检索索引。本稿用GEO统称，因为品牌面对的实务界面相同：引擎摄取什么、说出什么。**这些是作者术语约定，不是整个领域唯一标准。**

#### 2.2 研究已有认识

基础是Princeton GEO研究（Aggarwal，KDD2024），作者概括10,000查询、试内容改动，机器可提出处（引语统计引用）约提升25—40%。C-SEO Bench（Puerto2025）作为纠偏：多数会话SEO战术没用甚至伤害，来源相关性持续重要，故本文侧重源端页面质量，不玩回答端提示技巧。

三个引用研究相符：Kirsten显示生成搜索取更广异来源、内部知识依赖不同；Yang约366,000引用显示媒体集中、平台一致低；Algaba显示模型偏好高引来源。共同解释网上存在感强者最常被引，小品牌要爬这座山。

### 3 Ranqo平台

#### 3.1 查询层

每品牌生成六类自然语言提示，通过官方API发五引擎。模型选每家可联网生产类别，具体版本未报。Gemini/Perplexity/Grok每次联网；ChatGPT/Claude为控费每品牌每周冷却搜索，其间只靠参数，形成后续搜索开关对照。

作者说固定各家搜索支持型号可保持比较、让差异反映摄取检索而非包装；其他配置外推待未来。**校读：两个引擎部分运行关闭检索、另三个总开，并非全部同条件；类别名也不是固定精确版本，跨平台结论需保留此差。**

位置能原生传参的ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity用geo参数，否则Gemini/Grok用系统提示后缀。

**表1：模型类别（不是版本）、网页搜索政策、引用接口。**

|引擎|类别|搜索政策|引用面|
|---|---|---|---|
|ChatGPT|GPT-5|每品牌每周冷却|`annotations.url_citation`|
|Gemini|Gemini-3|始终grounded|`groundingChunks[].web`|
|Perplexity|Sonar|始终grounded，搜索原生|`search_results`数组|

#### 3.2 六类提示

同品牌可一类强、另一类近无，因此分别追踪。以跑鞋说明（仅翻译研究提示，不在这里给运动/医疗建议）：

- **发现：**漏斗顶部、未点名：“最好的跑鞋”“适合新手的好跑鞋”。
- **问题/解决：**具体难题：“脚踝痛该穿哪种跑鞋”“扁平足穿什么鞋”。
- **使用场景：**活动环境：“越野跑最佳鞋”“上班全天站立的鞋”。
- **比较：**权衡点名选项：“Nike Pegasus与Brooks Ghost”“马拉松Hoka还是Asics”。
- **专家：**深入技术：“稳定鞋适合何种前后落差”“碳板真能让我更快吗”。
- **品牌研究：**单一品牌：“Nike适合跑步吗”“Nike跑鞋评价”。

发现、问题/解决、场景、专家通常无品牌，测没人点名时会否冒出，属困难GEO发现任务；比较/品牌研究会点名，提及自然高，较少说明发现能力。新品牌起始集刻意无品牌。

**主题。**类别是单题形状，主题是上一层聚类（产品线、场景、竞争组、购买时机）。每主题批量生成且平衡类别，例如越野鞋、护士鞋，使跟踪由少题扩到广主题。

#### 3.3 引用提取

每回答提取：布尔`brandMentioned`、整数`brandPosition`（1/2/3…）、positive/neutral/negative标签、连续`sentimentScore∈[-1,1]`及承载情感的文字片段；所有grounding URL规范为域，分类news_media、community、review、video、social、developer、academic、government、reference、corporate。

来源—品牌关系标you、competitor、non_competitor、editorial、forum、review、social、reference、institutional、other；还提取竞争品牌名及位序数组。全部存单一（提示、平台、运行）元组。

#### 3.4 评分

提及、位序、情感行为不同，分开报告而非一权重混合。

1. **可见度：**每引擎提及/总提示×100。跨引擎权重ChatGPT.30、Gemini.20、Perplexity.20、Claude.20、Grok.10；按客户实际启用平台重新归一到1。
2. **平均位置：**只在提及题上平均位序，1是首个推荐，跨引擎同权。
3. **情感分：**(正面+.5×中性)/提及数×100；全正100、全中50、全负0，负面相对正面的损失是中性两倍。
4. **声量份额：**本品牌提及/(本品牌+竞争者提及)。竞争者需反复出现或解析到真实域，避免一次幻觉名字扩大分母。

每完成运行计算；单查询失败沿用上次值并标记，避免瞬时API错误看成下降。类别仅分项，不作聚合权重。等级A+≥90、A≥80、B+≥70、B≥60、C+≥50、C≥40、D≥30、F<30。系数在配置，易重新赋权。

#### 3.5 六维页面审计

每项0—100，合加权总页分：

1. **可抓取：**robots、sitemap、canonical、HTTPS、JS渲染、移动友好，能否到达解析。
2. **内容质量：**词数、可读性、段落、标题层级、内链、新鲜度。
3. **速度：**作者列Core Web Vitals LCP/FID/CLS；这是原文列表，本稿未核对现行标准。
4. **AI就绪：**实体清楚、结构化答案、行内引用、证据密度、出处标记，能否直接提答案。
5. **引用潜力：**具体可引单元（数字、定义、具名主张）、归因、数据可用。
6. **权威信任：**可见作者、资历、域权威、主题深度、E-E-A-T。

后三个GEO维度总权重最大，衡量事实清楚、证据可引、作者可见，作者认为与基础GEO出处信号相符。论文未给各维具体权重值，不补造。

#### 3.6 闭环建议引擎

Claude Sonnet温度.5、结构输出校验，读趋势、类别表现、内容缺口、竞争威胁、情感、可选GA4，输出排序`ImprovementRecommendation`行，含类别、动作、优先级、影响/工作量各1—3。

每行有目标维`baselineScore/currentScore/scoreDelta`；实施后复审差值可观测，是v1.1 RCT的闭环基础，不等于已证明真实引流提升。

#### 3.7 诊断到AI优化内容

内容管线读同上下文（永不出现提示、竞争优势、弱类别、审计缺口），输出有标题、角度、精确目标提示、优先级的内容brief，倾向现不可见主题而非泛扩张。

分工代理：brief排名主题，draft写文，humanization改自然语气，optimization评分既有页提定点改动；确定性阶段附Article+FAQPage JSON-LD。代理按六维信号设计，实体先开头、可引统计具名主张、FAQ、结构标题，作者称内容为AI引用而建，不只好读。

这是“行动”半环：诊断、发布、复测。机制在此描述，但生成内容是否因果提升引用，留待P3/P7，本文不声称。

#### 3.8 规模与重复单位

单位（品牌、提示、平台、运行）。品牌P题、五引擎每日，5P元组/天，约150P/月。

### 4 方法

#### 4.1 提示构造

Claude Sonnet温度.7，以品类、关键词、位置、覆盖（全球/国家/本地）、30天市场研究上下文生成。上下文带当前问题与竞争框架，避免静态词表。生成遵循类别混合（原文称Σ=1、引用3.4），控制难度1—5及搜索量估计1—5，分别反映专业程度、常见程度，兼顾头部和长尾。**搜索量是生成器估计，不是已观测真实搜索量；原文3.4实际列平台权重，未公开类别混合数值。**

默认不含品牌及别名，测泛品类可见度。仅用户主动选择比较/品牌研究才生成点名题。

#### 4.2 可见度、位置、情感

q发平台p得R(q,p)：

\[
m(q,p)\in\{fr,t3,m,i,none\},\quad \pi(q,p)\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\},\quad
\sigma(q,p)\in\{pos,neut,neg\},\quad S(q,p)=\{(url,domain,type,mb)\}.
\]

m依次first_rec首推、top_three前三、mentioned提及、indirect间接、none无；π位序，σ情感，S引用集。原文未在此展开mb字段。

\[
V_p(Q)=\frac{|\{q\in Q:m(q,p)\ne none\}|}{|Q|}.\tag{1}
\]
\[

\]
\[
SoV_p(b)=\frac{M(b,p)}{M(b,p)+\sum_{c\in C(b)}M(c,p)}.\tag{3}

#### 4.3 来源重合

由S得引用域集合Dp(q)，两平台Jaccard：

\[
J(p,p';q)=\frac{|D_p(q)\cap D_{p'}(q)|}{|D_p(q)\cup D_{p'}(q)|}.\tag{4}
\]

跨平台一致度是所有平台对、提示的平均J。论文未给两集合都空的处理规则，不补造。

#### 4.4 闭环提升

建议r作用URL u的维d：(b(r)=s_d(u,t_0)\)、(c(r)=s_d(u,t_1)\)、
\[

\]

#### 4.5 统计约定

均值/斜率用10,000有放回非参数bootstrap。三档用Kruskal–Wallis总体、Mann–Whitney U两两+Bonferroni、Cohen d，Tier1留一敏感。每品牌—引擎对运行序号拟OLS可见度斜率，再跨品牌平均+bootstrapCI。因为品牌分布有界右偏非正态，偏好非参数检验。

### 5 参照研究：2026年1月CRM五平台

先近看一品类。作者已发CRM研究：50个无品牌提示涵盖六类，五引擎各十次，2500回答、9600余品牌提及，十品牌Salesforce、HubSpot、Zoho、Pipedrive、Freshsales、Monday Sales CRM、Copper、Insightly、Capsule、Close。

头部集中：Salesforce/HubSpot/Zoho合计51%提及，底部Copper/Insightly/Capsule每五答不足一答出现。各引擎谁排前也不同。

**表2：仅提及时的平均位置，越低越好。**原表只列四品牌，另外六个不补造。

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|Salesforce|1.2|1.3|1.4|1.8|2.1|
|HubSpot|1.5|2.0|1.8|1.3|1.9|
|Zoho|3.1|3.8|3.5|2.4|3.2|

### 6 生产实证发现

2026年3—5月五引擎102品牌、3508完成运行、102,025回答、约15,815品牌提及、149,912来源引用。六项发现先报有推断支持的地位阶梯，再首日、类别、轨迹、来源、情感；所有数字由生产SQL，方法附录述。

#### 6.1 品牌地位阶梯

作者称地位是首日可见度主要决定因素，每降一档无品牌可见度差约30百分点：73%、44%、11%；在所查基准未见相近多客户量化。横截面观察，地位非随机，报告量化而非因果。

**首日。**每品牌第一次完成追踪、只无品牌品类题；含品牌题人为抬高，只辅助对比。

|档|n|无品牌可见度|95%CI|全部提示*|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Tier1|11|72.9%|[60.1,84.2]|73.5%|
|Tier2|36|43.6%|[36.4,50.9]|52.2%|
|Tier3|55|11.4%|[4.2,20.3]|17.3%|

*全部含约9%点名题，如“Razorpay做什么”，每引擎≥94%识别。Tier2抬8.6pp最大，因点名覆盖多；Tier1本来高，仅+.6pp。

品牌队列级10,000 bootstrap无品牌CI。Kruskal–Wallis H=38.32、df2、p=4.78×10⁻⁹。两两Mann–Whitney原文称在α=.05/3的Bonferroni下皆通过，并报告校正p：

|对比|U|p_Bonf|Cohen d|
|---|---|---|---|
|1对2|343|8.1×10⁻⁴|1.57|
|1对3|575|8.3×10⁻⁶|2.34|

### 7 讨论

#### 7.1 尤其给小品牌的四个实践结论

1. **花GEO预算前知道所在档。**不同档需要不同方案，作者声明以下是与数据相符假设，非已建立商业主张。Tier1首日73%近饱和，n11让强子结论脆弱，关注竞争声量而非基础识别。Tier2为44%，作者称绝对空间最大，但无干预基线平/降，不会自己升，定向干预能否关闭差距待P3。Tier3为11%，观察最快者也只涨10—20绝对点，作者建议先投资品牌规模（Wikipedia、主流报道、持续YouTube）跨到Tier2，再重平台细优化；具体行业看其SaaS/DTC指南。**这不是随机实验已证实的投放顺序；从11到100的算术空间其实比44到100大，“最大空间”是作者商业解释。**
2. **每引擎当独立市场。**来源重合低，Yang366k新闻与本102025品牌回答都见差异；Perplexity胜利不自动转Gemini，平台玩法不同。
3. **事实放前，而不是只堆schema。**基础GEO中引语统计引用带大提升，作者称重schema单独效应小，但P4尚要验证。行动是关键事实清楚提前，具体因素见其文章。
4. **闭环按周，不按季度。**作者由首日识别解释既有品牌数日识别、新实体更久，建议改后14—30天复审迭代。**本数据没测从发布到识别时延，也没比较复审间隔，故窗口是建议而非已验证最佳周期。**

#### 7.2 诚实的因果地位

实证只报基线、轨迹、来源/情感构成，不报建议引擎RCT。

支持：分档阶梯、首日识别、稳定格、来源构成、情感份额，是生产遥测直接读数。

假设：定向内容投资能抬Tier3品牌规模天花板，需要RCT。

尚不支持：Ranqo建议导致品牌可见度具体提升。数据模型有闭环结构，不等群体闭环效果已测，P3后续。

最清楚建立的是首日三档差、Tier1留一稳健。干预是否加速轨迹待RCT，不预承诺未从受控实验得到的倍数。

#### 7.3 白帽测量说明

Ranqo只测和建议页质量，不生成隐藏文字、排名攻击载荷、骗引擎内容，建议引擎被要求拒绝。作者认为投机收益短、下次模型更新会逆转，真实质量可持续，这是本文唯一认可优化。此为立场，不是本文对所有更新的实验验证。

### 8 限制

1. **建议引擎无因果声称。**轨迹为观察基线非处理效果，闭环客户测量未来P3。
2. **便利样本。**偏SaaS、零售执行、金融科技、印度DTC，不代表所有品类。Tier1 n11，Agency引擎Claude/Grok品牌更少；报告n、小样警示。
3. **人工地位。**Wikipedia、新闻、融资本就网上显著性代理，阶梯是预期效应大小量化，不是显著性因果独立证明。规则/名单附录B，双人一致未来；Tier1留一70.5—76.7%。
4. **平台不透明。**所有从API输出推断，无内部摄取、保留、检索视角。
5. **每引擎一型号。**搜索支持生产变体固定，其他配置能否复现阶梯未测。
6. **情感启发式。**模型分类含品牌片段，45.5%翻转混合真实输出与分类器噪声，未分离。

### 9 结论与未来

102品牌中地位是首日可见度主导因素。五引擎来源、位置、情感不同，作者称对schema、作者署名、时效、检索grounding反应不同；但本版对这些分项的因果测试尚属计划，应结合7.2读。

无品牌可见度大多保持，ChatGPT/Perplexity缓降。实践需分引擎测、作用可保留的上游信号、按周复测；作者称季度对“在自身输出上再训练”的媒介太慢。**本研究没有内部训练数据，不能据此断言具体引擎会把这些回答重新训练。**

三条未来：多厂商复现；按基础GEO形式在品牌队列随机处理/对照建议的P3，报告真正可期待的实施提升；把P6训练/检索分离推广成公开基准。

实务文献落后于数据，学术文献又分化快过单团队综合。作者认为2026最有用是发可运行方案与可重新评分数字，使主张被证伪而非重复。

## 第二部分：详细讲解与小白实操

这里把论文变成你可操作的测量练习。示范品牌“青禾”与数字为虚构；没有使用任何商业服务，也没改动网站。

### 1 最容易把分数测高的方法，也是最没用的发现测试

问“青禾报销软件怎么样”，AI回答里当然很可能有青禾；问“20人团队如何选择报销工具”，才是在没人点名时会不会主动想到你。本文两者分别约94—100%和12—52%，不是同一个成绩。

建立题库第一步就分两栏：**带品牌题**用于品牌信息、评价、误解诊断；**不带品牌题**用于自然发现。不要把它们混起来宣传“AI可见度97%”。同理比较题若“青禾对其他”，已经送了名字，不能与无品牌发现题公平比。

六类可写：发现“适合小团队的报销工具”；问题“报销经常漏审批怎样处理”；场景“远程团队如何收票”；专家“多级审批权限怎样设计”；比较“青禾与某真实替代方案差异”；品牌研究“青禾支持哪些功能”。具体功能答案必须来自真实文档，本教学不假造。

### 2 “第一天就认识”不能证明新品牌一天进模型

论文的第一天是客户第一次点跟踪按钮。Nike此前已存在多年，AI第一次被测就认识它并不意外。要研究新品牌多久出现，需要知道品牌/页面发布时刻，连续固定提示观察，并区分联网和不联网。

因此这篇能反驳“所有开始测的品牌都要等半年才出现”这种宽泛说法，却不能证明“我今天发一篇明天就被模型记住”。14—30天复审是作者建议，不是已测得索引时延保证。

### 3 看懂73、44、11的价值与限制

阶梯说明现有品牌规模与无品牌出现率强相关，很适合设合理基线：小品牌与Nike比绝对率很难有意义。先找同品类、同规模的对照，再看目标问题中的变化。

但档位本身用Wikipedia、媒体、融资编码，这些就是网上知名度的代理。不能说这套表独立证明“买媒体报道就升33个百分点”。11→44不是某项服务套餐的收益承诺。Wikipedia不是可任意创建的营销位，论文只把百科覆盖当已有地位信号，未测试付费内容可造成跨档。

Tier1只有11品牌，留一检查说明单个品牌不主导均值，不解决人为档位的所有主观性；正式双人编码还未做。统计显著证明组间有差，不证明差来自哪一因素。

### 4 平均可见度、位置、声量如何算

假设10题里青禾出现3题，则可见度30%。三次位置1、3、5，平均位置3；其余七次没出现，不参加位置均值。因此位置3不能单独说明表现好，可能90%题完全消失还偶尔第一。

青禾提及3次、甲5次、乙2次，SoV=3/(3+5+2)=30%。若漏掉乙，变37.5%；换竞争清单数字就变，必须固定并列明名单。模型幻觉的品牌名先核实，不能随便加进分母。

跨引擎加权也要公开。假设只跑ChatGPT和Perplexity，原权重.3/.2重新归一为.6/.4；若提及率20%与40%，合成28%。后来加一个低率引擎，总分变不必是内容退步，可能权重和平台集合变了。最稳先看每引擎原始率，再看固定权重综合。

类别宏平均与提示微平均也不同：一个品牌1000题、另一个10题，宏平均每品牌同权，微平均大题库更重。表3是先每品牌类内率，再跨品牌平均，不能用102025回答总数当每个格的独立样本量。

### 5 为什么本篇“很稳定”，论文14又说不要只测一次？

两篇对象、样本和规则不同。本文大量小品牌，在很多题里三次或多次都没出现，63.2%从不，把全体推向“稳定”。论文14关注来源集合和品牌匹配的不同重复集，不应硬当互相推翻。

有限三次没出现仍不能证明真实概率0。若真实率20%，三次全没出现概率.8³=51.2%。原平台查询失败还沿用旧值，这有助界面连续，却可能使观测更平；本篇未公开失败比例及是否在稳定性分析排除沿用值。

所以小白不应学成“问一次足够”。对重要题重复并存原答，标采集失败、沿用、真实零提及。三个运行可起步检出明显变化，不保证精确提及率；想估小幅改善需要更多独立信息和稳定测量条件。

### 6 6.7倍到底是什么，不是什么

它只是两种模式占比45.5%/6.8%≈6.69。情感模式筛“至少3次提及”，提及模式筛“至少3次运行”；一个只在被提及后研究，另一个含从不出现，分母不同。它不是同一随机变量的方差比，也不是所有品牌都需要6.7倍预算。

情感有分类器噪声：回答“适合小团队，但不适合复杂合规场景”可被不同判定器标正、中、负。应保存含品牌原句和上下文，人工复核负面/翻转样本，分别记录真实批评、适用条件、事实错误，别把“并非所有人适用”全当负面危机。

“始终负面0%”只表示入样格没观察到，不能承诺AI不会形成持续负评。对重要事实错误，核原来源并改善可核验信息，比追逐单次情感分更有意义。

### 7 来源分类有两个坐标，别混成同一渠道

一个竞争公司的“最佳报销工具”文章，**站点类型**是企业，**页面类型**是榜单。这就是企业占78%和内容占59%能同时成立，并不矛盾。自家站仅2.9%也不等于“官网没用”：样本是含品牌提及答案的全部引用，多个同行页可能占大，而你的官网仍是事实核验入口。

榜单占全部21%与占内容35.7%是同件事两分母，.59×.357≈.211。不能说全部35.7%都是榜单，更不能说写榜单有21%被引概率；研究没把没被引的所有榜单纳分母。

实际动作：从与你有关的回答收集来源，标自家/同行/媒体/社区/视频，再标产品页/指南/比较/榜单。看哪些具体问题缺你能提供的证据，再决定内容形式。别根据这个SaaS、印度DTC偏重样本直接断言所有行业都应先拍视频再做论坛。

### 8 六维审计怎样变成具体修改

先看能否抓取、主体是否真实可读、规范地址是否一致；再看内容是否回答真实任务。为“青禾报销流程”页做一个可复核清单：

|维度|检查动作|可保存证据|
|---|---|---|
|可抓取|检查公开页能读取关键正文、规范URL与索引指令|页面HTML/响应记录|
|内容质量|看每节能否回答一个真实子问题，是否重复空话|改前后段落|
|速度|用已有测量工具记录加载表现，按当前工具口径|测量报告与时间|
|AI就绪|首段说明实体、适用范围、核心答案|首段与问题对应表|
|引用潜力|定义、规则、示例、数字有证据可查|来源链接与日期|
|权威信任|作者、经验、审核/更新说明真实可见|署名资历与责任说明|

分数可帮助发现缺口，但作者没公开维度权重、评分验证，因此不复制一个“权威分90即可引用”的门槛。Schema帮助表达数据，不保证引用；P4近零效应仍待测试，不能从本文得“schema完全无用”。

### 9 建立一次不会被平台配置误导的复测

固定一批无品牌题、地区、语言、产品/API、精确可得型号、是否联网；把点名题分开。每次记录运行时间、原答、提及、位置、引用、情感原句、成功/失败。模型版本不公开就记未知。

本文三个引擎每次联网、两个每周才联网，跨平台比较有模式差；你复测时至少分别报search-on/off，而不是合成一列。关闭联网后答对实体，也不能直接定位“训练层已记住”：可能还有系统上下文或其他产品机制，API输出不能揭示内部全部来源。

改稿先挑最明确缺口，保留未改页或题作对照，记录发布日期。复测周期按实际更新与数据量决定，14—30天可作作者建议的观察窗口，不能等同平台承诺。不要把每运行−1.34%解释成每天必跌1.34%；运行频率不同，且提示集变化可能造成斜率。

### 10 审计分改善，不等真实可见度改善

例如标题更清楚让内部AI就绪分60→80，ℓ=20。那只证明评分规则给了20分，不证明平台提及率提高20个百分点。要完成闭环，还要再问固定题，观察真实答案；最好有随机对照或明确准实验，区分同时发生的其他变化。

本篇P3/P7恰是要解决这件事，尚无结果。厂商作者持股、数据代码不公开，不意味着数据必错，但意味着我们不能独立核验，也不能把它当服务效果的独立证明。引用时连同利益声明和非因果范围一起保存。

### 11 你能从本篇真正带走的交付物

能交出一套分点名/未点名、分六类的题库；固定平台/联网条件的观测表；同时报告出现率、仅出现时名次、固定竞争集SoV；一份来源双坐标分类；一份有真实依据的页面改动记录；再给出带样本和不确定性的复测。

自测：问“青禾怎么样”提青禾算发现成功吗？不算。已知品牌首测识别等于新品牌一天收录吗？不等于。榜单21%等于写榜单被引概率21%吗？不是。内部页面分+20就代表GEO增长20吗？不是。某格三次没提能证明永远没提吗？不能。

brand is mentioned at all.

1 Introduction
More and more, people get their answers straight from
an AI assistant instead of scrolling through ten blue links.
They ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, or Grok
what to buy, what tool to use, or who to trust, and they act
on what comes back. For a brand, this quietly changes the
question that matters. The old question was whether you
rank for a keyword. The new question is whether an AI
model, when someone asks about your category, actually
names you.
This is what GEO is about. Generative Engine Opti-
mization (GEO) is the practice of measuring and improving
how AI search engines represent, cite, and recommend
a brand (Aggarwal et al., 2024). Two related terms get
used alongside it: Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)
and AI Search Visibility. We treat both as part of the
broader GEO scope in this paper, because they describe
the same job from slightly different angles. GEO is also
not a replacement for SEO. It is built on top of good SEO,
since the content an AI engine ingests is, for the most part,
the content you already publish for search.
There is one more thing worth saying up front. The
brands that are already big and authoritative tend to get
cited no matter what. The hard, unsolved problem belongs
to everyone else: the SMEs, the D2C brands, the creators,
the early-stage startups, and any brand without much of
an online footprint. That is the audience we care about
most, and the gap this paper sets out to measure.
A growing body of academic work already tells us
that the AI-search playbook is not the old SEO playbook.
Generative engines pull from a broader and very different
set of sources than classical search, and they lean on their
own internal knowledge to different degrees (Kirsten et
al., 2025). When they do cite, the citations concentrate on
a small set of outlets, and different engines pick different
outlets (Yang, 2025). LLMs also reward sources that are
already widely cited, a Matthew effect that makes the rich
richer (Algaba et al., 2025). And the first careful benchmark
of “conversational SEO” tactics found that most of them
do not help, and several actively hurt (Puerto et al., 2025).
We build on these findings with production data.
What this paper contributes.
1. A way to measure AI brand visibility in produc-
tion. We describe Ranqo (also Ranqo AI), a platform
that issues controlled queries to five AI engines and
measures, for each brand, whether the engines mention
it, where they rank it, how they frame it, and its share
of voice against competitors. It classifies the sources
behind those answers, runs a six-dimension page audit,
and re-measures on a recurring cadence.
2. A category reference study. We summarize Ranqo’s
published CRM study (Ranqo, 2026b): 50 unbranded
prompts sent to all five engines ten times each (2,500
responses) across ten CRM brands.

2 Background and Related Work
2.1 SEO, AEO, GEO, and AI Visibility
A handful of terms now describe overlapping work, so
we fix what we mean by each, following the practitioner
usage in (Ranqo, 2026a,c). SEO is about blue-link ranking
on classical search engines. AEO is about being the single
source a featured snippet or direct-answer box pulls from.
GEO is about being cited and recommended when a
large language model synthesizes an answer across many
sources. AI Visibility is the broader question of whether
an entity is represented inside a model’s parameters and
retrieval indexes at all. In this paper we use GEO as the
umbrella term and keep AEO and AI Visibility under it,
because for a brand the practical surface is the same: what
the engines ingest, and what they say back.
2.2 What the research already shows
The academic picture is young but consistent on a few
points, and we lean on it throughout.
The foundational benchmark is the Princeton GEO
study (Aggarwal et al., 2024) (KDD 2024), which ran
10,000 queries and tested content changes for their effect
on whether an answer cites a page. The biggest wins
came from adding machine-extractable provenance: quota-
tions, statistics, and citations, each worth roughly 25–40%
more visibility. That is still the core of the modern GEO
playbook.
The most useful corrective is C-SEO Bench (Puerto
et al., 2025), the first systematic benchmark of “conversa-
tional SEO” tactics. Its headline is blunt: most of those
tactics do not help, and several hurt, while plain source
relevance keeps working. This shapes how we run our
own experiments. We test changes to page-quality signals
on the source side, not prompt-engineering tricks on the
response.

3 The Ranqo Platform
3.1 Platform query layer
For each tracked brand, Ranqo generates a set of natural-
language prompts spanning six categories (discovery,
problem_solution, comparison, use_case, expert, and
brand_research) and issues each prompt to all five en-
gines via official APIs. Table 1 summarizes the per-engine
configuration.
Model selection.
For each engine we query its cur-
rent search-enabled production model (Table 1) — the
variant that exposes web retrieval through the normal
API. Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok are grounded on every
query; ChatGPT and Claude run web search on a weekly
cooldown per brand to control cost, and between those
passes they answer from their parameters alone — the
search-on/search-off contrast we use in §6.1. Holding
the search-enabled variant constant across engines keeps
the setup comparable, so the cross-engine results in §6.1
reflect how the engines ingest and retrieve rather than
how they bundle search; how far the patterns generalize
to other model configurations is left to future work (§8).
Per-brand location is passed as a native geo parameter
where the API supports one (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity)
and as a system-prompt suffix otherwise (Gemini, Grok).
3.2 The six prompt categories
The six categories are not interchangeable. A brand can
look strong in one and be almost invisible in another, so
we track all six separately. Using running shoes as the
example throughout:
Discovery Broad, top-of-funnel questions where the
buyer is still exploring and names no brand. “best run-
ning shoes,” “good running shoes for beginners.”
Problem/solution The buyer has a specific problem and
wants something that fixes it. “I have ankle pain, what
kind of running shoes should I wear,” “shoes for flat feet.”
Use case A specific activity or setting. “best shoes for
trail running,” “shoes for standing all day at work.”
Comparison Weighing named options against each other.
“Nike Pegasus vs Brooks Ghost,” “Hoka or Asics for a
marathon.” These usually name brands.
Expert Deeper, more technical questions from an in-
formed buyer. “what heel-to-toe drop suits a stability shoe,”
“does a carbon plate actually make me faster.”
Brand research Questions about one named brand. “is
Nike a good running brand,” “Nike running shoes reviews.”
These name the brand by definition.
The split matters for measurement. The first four
(discovery, problem/solution, use case, and expert) are
normally unbranded, so they test whether an engine
surfaces the brand when nobody has named it. That is
the hard, GEO-relevant case, and it is the one we lean
on throughout the paper. Only comparison and brand
research name a brand, which makes a mention much
more likely and tells us far less about discovery. For that
reason the starter set we generate for a new brand is
deliberately unbranded.
Prompt themes.
Categories describe the shape of a
single prompt. Themes sit one level up. A theme is a topical
cluster (a product line, a use-case area, a competitor set, a
buying occasion), and the platform generates a batch of
prompts under each theme while keeping the category mix
balanced inside it. Themes let a brand track a whole topic
at once (say, “trail running shoes” or “shoes for nurses”)
instead of writing prompts one at a time, which is how
tracking scales from a handful of prompts to broad topic
coverage.
3.3 Citation extraction
For each engine response, Ranqo extracts:
• Brand-mention signals: a Boolean brandMentioned,
an integer brandPosition (1st, 2nd, 3rd, ...), a senti-
ment label (positive / neutral / negative) accompanied by
a continuous sentimentScore ∈[−1, 1] and an array
of sentiment-bearing text spans.
• Source citations: every URL the engine grounded the
answer on, normalized to canonical domain and classi-
fied into a type (news_media, community, review, video,
social, developer, academic, government, reference, cor-
porate).
• Source-to-brand relationship: each cited source is la-
beled as you, competitor, non_competitor, editorial, forum,
review, social, reference, institutional, or other.
• Competitor mentions: an array of competitor names
with their ordinal positions.
All signals are stored at the level of a single (prompt,
platform, run) tuple.

3.5 Six-dimension page audit
In parallel with the query layer, Ranqo runs a six-
dimension page audit against each tracked URL, scor-
ing each dimension 0–100 and combining them into a
weighted overall page score:
1. Crawlability — whether an AI crawler can reach and
parse the page at all: robots, sitemap, canonical, HTTPS,
JS rendering, and mobile-friendly checks.
2. Content Quality — whether the page is substantive
and well-structured: word count, readability, paragraph
structure, heading hierarchy, internal linking, and fresh-
ness.
3. Page Speed — how quickly the page loads for users
and crawlers: Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS).
4. AI Readiness — how easily a model can lift a direct an-
swer from the page: entity clarity, structured answers,
inline citations, evidence density, and provenance mark-
ers.
5. Citation Potential — whether the page offers some-
thing concrete worth quoting: quotability units (num-
bers, definitions, named claims), source attribution, and
data availability.
6. Authority & Trust — whether the page signals credible,
first-hand expertise: visible author byline, credentials,
domain authority, topical depth, and E-E-A-T mark-
ers (Ranqo, 2026h).
Together, the three GEO-specific dimensions (AI Readi-
ness, Citation Potential, and Authority & Trust) carry
the largest share of the page score and are the ones most
specific to GEO: they score whether a page states its facts
clearly, backs them with quotable evidence, and makes
its authorship visible. These line up with the content-
provenance signals the Princeton benchmark found most
effective (Aggarwal et al., 2024).
3.6 Closed-loop recommendation engine
For every brand, Ranqo’s recommendation engine (Claude
Sonnet, temperature 0.5, with structured-output vali-
dation) ingests visibility trends, category performance,
content gaps, competitor threats, sentiment distribution,
and optional GA4 traffic context, and emits a ranked list
of ImprovementRecommendation rows. Each row carries
a category, an action type, a priority class, and two scores
on a 1–3 scale (impact, effort).
Each recommendation also carries baselineScore,
currentScore, and scoreDelta on the dimension it
targets. When the recommendation is implemented and
re-audited, the delta becomes observable. This is the
closed-loop primitive the v1.1 RCT (Protocol P3, §6.7) is
built on.

4 Methodology
4.1 Prompt construction
Prompts are generated by Claude Sonnet (temperature
0.7) seeded with the brand’s category, keywords, location,
reach (worldwide / country / local), and 30-day market-
research context. The market-research context seeds
the generator with the live questions and competitor

a static keyword list. Generation honors a category

produces unbranded prompts, keeping the brand name
and its aliases out of the prompt text. This is what lets
us measure generic category visibility rather than self-
referential mentions, and it is the unbranded measure
we lean on throughout the paper. Branded prompts
are produced only when a user explicitly opts into the
comparison or brand-research categories.

4.5 Statistical conventions
Uncertainty on means and slopes is reported with a non-
parametric bootstrap (10,000 resamples with replacement).
For the three-tier visibility comparison (§6.1) we use a
Kruskal–Wallis omnibus test across tiers, followed by pair-
wise Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction
and Cohen’s d as the effect size, and we check the small
Tier 1 cell with a leave-one-out sensitivity. Per-engine
trajectories (§6.4) are summarized by an ordinary-least-
squares slope of visibility on run index, fit per (brand,
engine) and averaged across brands with a bootstrap CI.
We prefer nonparametric tests because the per-brand visi-
bility distributions are bounded and right-skewed rather
than normal.

The category is top-heavy. Salesforce, HubSpot, and

6.8 Summary
Table 4 collects the six reported findings and the seven
designed-but-unrun protocols. The headline and statisti-
cally strongest result is the brand-stature visibility ladder
(§6.1): on each brand’s first tracking run, unbranded cat-
egory visibility is 73% for Tier 1 brands, 44% for Tier 2,
and 11% for Tier 3 — about 30 percentage points per step
down. Because stature is observed rather than randomized,
we report it as a multi-tenant quantification of an expected
effect rather than a novel discovery.
Three further results are descriptive contributions
the existing literature does not supply. The source-class
decomposition (§6.5) finds the brand’s own domain is only
2.9% of citations, video is the largest non-corporate source,
and the listicle is the single most-cited content format. The
mention-determinism / runs-to-stability result (§6.4) finds
AI surfacing is near-binary — 77.5% of (brand, prompt,
engine) cells are strictly always- or never-mentioned —
and that, left alone, unbranded visibility holds on most
engines and drifts down only slowly on ChatGPT and
Perplexity. And the 6.7× sentiment-vs-mention noise
gap (§6.6) shows the two signals cannot share one noise
budget. Two supporting findings complete the set: day-1
recognition (§6.2), where a brand surfaces immediately
when a prompt names it but far less when it does not,
reported with explicit limits on what it supports; and
the prompt-category split (§6.3), where broad discovery
questions surface a brand most (∼23%) and specific
problem and use-case questions least (∼11%). The
protocols (P1–P7, §6.7) are a research agenda, not results,
and are not claimed as contributions of this paper.
7 Discussion
7.1 Four practical conclusions, especially for smaller
brands
1. Know which tier you are in before you spend on
GEO. The right GEO program looks different in each
tier; we frame these as hypotheses consistent with the
data, not established commercial claims. Tier 1 global
brands sit at 73% day-1 visibility, effectively at satura-
tion (the n = 11 Tier-1 cell makes strong sub-claims
fragile); their need is share-of-voice against competi-
tors rather than basic recognition. Tier 2 brands sit at
44% with the largest absolute headroom, but the no-
intervention baseline (§6.4) shows unbranded visibility
drifting flat-to-down rather than climbing on its own;
whether targeted intervention closes that headroom is
the v1.1 RCT question (Protocol P3), not a baseline find-
ing. Tier 3 brands sit at 11%; the fastest Tier-3 movers
we observed (§6.1) still travel only 10–20 absolute points
across the window, so the highest-confidence move is
brand-mass investment (Wikipedia, mainstream press,
sustained YouTube presence) to clear the Tier 2 thresh-
old before running heavy per-engine optimization. The
specifics differ by sector; see our SaaS playbook (Ranqo,
2026f) and DTC guide (Ranqo, 2026g).
2. Treat each engine as a separate market. Cross-
platform source overlap is low. Yang et al. (Yang, 2025)
found this across 366,000 news citations; we find the
same pattern across 102,025 brand-tracking responses.
A Perplexity win does not transfer to Gemini, and
the working playbook for each engine differs accord-
ingly (Ranqo, 2026e).
3. Put your facts up front, not your schema markup.
Aggarwal et al. (2024) showed that content-quality addi-
tions (quotations, statistics, citations) drive the largest
GEO lifts. Heavy structured-data markup, by contrast,
does little on its own, which is what Protocol P4 sets out
to confirm. The practical move is to state your key facts
clearly and early on the page, where the engine is most
likely to read them; the page-level factors that most
affect whether a brand gets cited are detailed in (Ranqo,
2026d).
4. Close the loop in weeks, not quarters. Our day-1
recognition finding (§6.2) shows established brands are
recognized within days, while brand-new entities take
longer. Either way the loop runs on weeks: make a
change, then re-audit and iterate at 14–30 days.
7.2 The honest causal status of this dataset
The empirical section reports baselines, trajectories, and
source and sentiment composition. It does not report a
randomized controlled trial of the recommendation engine.
We separate three claim tiers carefully.
What the data supports. The per-tier visibility ladder,
the day-1 recognition, the deterministic-cell finding, and
the source-composition and sentiment shares. These are
direct readings of production telemetry.
What the data hypothesizes. That the Tier 3 brand-mass
ceiling can be lifted with targeted content investment. This
is a hypothesis derived from the data; it needs RCT-grade
validation.
What the data does not yet support: any causal claim
that Ranqo’s recommendations cause a measured visibility
lift on a brand. The recommendation engine’s closed-
loop machinery is built into the data model (§3.6), but
population-scale closed-loop measurement is left to v1.1
(Protocol P3).
What it most clearly establishes. The sharp three-tier
day-1 visibility ladder of §6.1 (robust to the Tier-1 leave-
one-out reclassification). Whether intervention accelerates
those trajectories is the v1.1 RCT question (Protocol P3);
we do not pre-commit to a multiplier we have not derived
from a controlled experiment.

8 Limitations
We name the constraints on the empirical claims directly.
A reader should weigh the headline findings against this
list.
1. No causal claim on the recommendation engine.
Every trajectory in §6.1 is an observational baseline,
not a treatment effect; closed-loop measurement on
customer brands remains future work (Protocol P3).
2. Convenience-sampled cohort. The brands skew to-
ward SaaS, retail-execution, fintech, and Indian DTC, so
we do not claim category representativeness. Several
cuts run on small cells (the Tier 1 group is n = 11, and
the Agency-tier engines Grok and Claude run on far
fewer brands than the rest). We report n next to every
aggregate and flag small-sample readings.
3. Manual tier classification.
The tier assignment
is hand-coded from public signals of brand stature
(Wikipedia, press, funding). Because those signals are
themselves proxies for web prominence, the ladder
should be read as quantifying the size of an expected
effect, not as independent proof that prominence drives
citation. The rubric and rosters are in Appendix B; a
formal inter-rater check is left to v1.1. The day-1 lad-
der is robust to the reclassifications we tried (Tier-1
leave-one-out range [70.5, 76.7]%).
4. Platform opacity. Every result is inferred from API
outputs. We have no direct view into how the engines
ingest, retain, or retrieve.
5. One model variant per engine. We measure each
engine’s search-enabled production variant and hold it
fixed; whether the brand-stature ladder reproduces on
other model configurations is untested here.
6. Sentiment is a heuristic. Sentiment is classified by
a model on the spans that mention the brand, so the
45.5% sentiment-flip rate (§6.6) mixes genuine output
variance with classifier noise; we have not separated
the two.
9 Conclusion and Future Work
In our 102-brand cohort, brand stature is the dominant
determinant of day-1 AI visibility. The five engines diverge
on sources, position, and sentiment, and they respond
differently to schema markup, bylines, freshness, and
web-search grounding. On the trajectory side, unbranded
visibility mostly holds when a brand does nothing, drifting
down only slowly on ChatGPT and Perplexity over our
window. In practice, this means a brand’s GEO program
has to measure each engine separately, intervene on
the upstream signals the engines actually retain, and re-
measure on a cycle of weeks; a quarterly cadence is too
slow for a medium that re-trains on its own outputs.

web-search-on/off design (Protocol P6, §6.7) generalizes
to a public benchmark.
The practitioner literature in this space runs well
behind the data, and the academic literature is fragmenting
faster than any single team can synthesize it. We think the
most useful thing GEO research can do in 2026 is publish
protocols that others can run and numbers that others can
re-score, so that claims get falsified rather than repeated.
